t5.condition: prong A (pre-registered): median over 5 blocks of (slower baseline achieved / flashdb achieved) <= 1.5; prong B (ticket-80 cross-check): flashdb sustained the rung under the unified rule in at least 4 of 5 blocks
t5.reading_limit: with both arms paced at one offered rate, an achieved rate cannot exceed that rate, so a declared arm that holds the rung scores a deficit of at most 1.0526; read this PASS as non-inferiority at a paced rung, not as a throughput advantage
t5.threshold: T5 low-load non-inferiority: at the 1x rung flashdb must be within 1.5x of the slower baseline (2x is the fail line, 10x a design failure)

t6.condition: a level is common when every arm was OFFERED it (the pre-registration's wording); at the highest such level the NUMERATOR is flashdb's median achieved rate over the blocks it sustained that level in (null only when it sustained none) and the DENOMINATOR is the best baseline's same quantity. Two quantities, two rules: this numerator asks only whether any block sustained the level, while the stricter 'sustained in >= 4 of 5 blocks' rule governs `secondary_reading` -- the ratio of each arm's highest sustained LEVEL -- and never this ratio
t6.defect: at 200 rps flashdb sustained 200.0 rps and the best baseline (sqlite) sustained 200.0 rps: 1.0x against the required 3.0x -- and by construction: an achieved rate is bounded by the offered rate, so two arms that both sustain a common offered level differ by at most 0.0526 and the ratio cannot exceed 1.0526
t6.fix: add rungs BELOW the 50 rps floor so each baseline's sustained level exists, then read the ratio of the highest sustained LEVELS; the pre-registered throughput ratio at a common offered level is bounded by 1/SUSTAINED_TOLERANCE for any pair of arms and cannot reach 3x. Both are pre-registration changes and neither is made here

secondary_reading.metric: the ratio of each arm's highest sustained offered LEVEL (NOT the pre-registered throughput ratio: reported so a FAIL is not read as a measured shortfall)

t6.threshold: T6 high-load superiority: at the highest common offered level flashdb must reach at least 3x the best baseline's sustained throughput under the same latency rule

t7.condition: the declared arm's own T5 prongs at the 1x rung
t7.disclosure: flashdb-learned was not run: M1 wires no learner controller, so a second flashdb arm would measure the same declared wiring twice
t7.threshold: T7 initial-policy quality: the declared arm alone must pass T5
